title: Ice domain physical parameter guardrails — prevent silent extrapolation
reference: ISO 19906:2019 Annex C; Timco & Weeks (2010) Cold Regions Sci. Tech. 60(3):209-229; Riska et al. (1997) VTT Publ. 319; ITTC Ice Committee (2017); Schulson & Duval (2009) Creep and Fracture of Ice
method: Three-tier bound validation: hard bounds (physical impossibility → reject), soft bounds (calibration domain → warn), typical range (normal operation → pass). 8 ice parameters covered: thickness, strength, friction, speed, density, elastic modulus, Poisson's ratio, temperature.

method_selection.adopted: Static bound validation with dataclass-based parameter registry, validate/clamp/extrapolation-risk API, CLI entry point (tensorfvm-ice-guard)

rejected.schema-only validation (Pydantic): Catches type errors but not physically impossible values — this was the root cause of the original failure
rejected.dynamic bounds (temperature-dependent): More accurate but requires additional inputs; deferred to future work
rejected.correlation-aware validation: Would catch inconsistent parameter combinations (e.g., thick ice + low strength); requires joint probability models; deferred

verdict: PASS — 47/47 tests pass; specific failure cases (h=50m, σ_c=100 MPa) correctly rejected; CLI entry point functional

h_50m.error: ice_thickness (h) = 50.0 m is outside physical bounds [0.01, 10.0] m

sigma_c_100mpa.error: ice_strength (σ_c) = 100.0 MPa is outside physical bounds [0.1, 30.0] MPa
